title: Why compound interest feels like magic

clips.label: Golden hook
clips.vo: Put one hundred dollars away today. In forty years, it could be worth over two thousand. Without adding a single cent.
clips.visual: A piggy bank receives one coin; a counter races from 100 to 2,172 while the figure gasps.

clips.label: Disrupt
clips.vo: Most people think wealth comes from big wins. It mostly comes from small amounts, and a lot of time.
clips.visual: A lottery-style jackpot gets crossed out; a tiny coin and a long calendar take its place.

clips.label: Secret
clips.vo: Here is the trick. Your interest starts earning interest of its own, like a snowball rolling downhill.
clips.visual: The figure pushes a snowball off a hilltop; it rolls down and grows as it goes.

clips.label: Truth
clips.vo: In year one, you earn eight dollars. By year thirty, that same hundred earns over seventy dollars a year.
clips.visual: Two bars compare year 1 and year 30 interest; the figure points as the second bar towers.

clips.label: Truth II
clips.vo: The curve stays flat for years, then bends sharply upward. Most people quit right before the bend.
clips.visual: A growth curve draws itself; a figure walks along it and turns back just before the steep part.

clips.label: Elevation
clips.vo: The best time to start was yesterday. The second best time is today. So, what will you start compounding?
clips.visual: A seedling grows into a tree beside the figure; a question mark pops.
